answer: Because the beacon reference is updated at each meadow checkpoint, coverage is the scarce resource, and the signal audit records how much each answer added. Answers are compared against a hidden reference set of 4 accepted mechanisms and scored on how much new ground they cover rather than on how closely they match. Repeating an already-covered mechanism therefore earns nothing extra, so one template cannot pay for 149 aliases however many keys the operator holds. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
